h: The Four Divine Gifts and the Rectification of the Flood
Torah, suffering, sacrifice, and prayer are paths by which the blemishes of earlier generations are healed.
Torah and Afflictions as Remedies for Sin

p: בְּתַנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ א):
— In Midrash Tanchuma (Parashat Noach 1):
"אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ,
— ‘These are the generations of Noah,
יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים שֶׁבָּחַר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי
— blessed be the Name of the King of kings Who chose Israel, etc.,
וְנָתַן לָנוּ הַתּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי",
— and gave us the Torah, etc.’,
וְהֶאֱרִיךְ בִּשְׁבַח הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה;
— and elaborated upon the praise of the Oral Torah;
וּלְהָבִין הַשַּׁיָּיכוּת לְהַפָּרָשָׁה
— and to understand the connection to the parashah
וּלְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ".
— and to that which is stated: 'These are the generations of Noah.'
אָמְנָם אִיתָא (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ל)
— Indeed, it is brought in Midrash Rabbah (Shemot Rabbah, Parashah 30)
שֶׁבִּיקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיתֵּן לָהֶם לְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים:
— that the Holy One, blessed be He, sought to give the Generation of the Flood four things:
תּוֹרָה, וְיִסּוּרִין, וַעֲבוֹדַת קָרְבָּנוֹת, וּתְפִלָּה,
— Torah, afflictions, the service of sacrificial offerings, and prayer,
וְלֹא בִּקְשׁוּ וְכוּלֵי.
— yet they did not desire them, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רָצָה לַהֲשִׁיבָם לַמּוּטָב
— Namely, Hashem willed to return them to goodness
וְלָתֵת עֵצוֹת נֶגֶד יֵצֶר לֵב הָאָדָם רַע מִנְּעֻרָיו.
— and to provide remedies against the evil inclination of man's heart from his youth.
וְיִסּוּרִין הֵם כַּפָּרָה עַל הֶעָבָר,
— And afflictions serve as atonement for the past,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ד.)
— as they stated (Avodah Zarah 4a)
עַל פָּסוּק "רַק אֶתְכֶם יָדַעְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר":
— on the verse 'Only you have I known, etc.':
אוֹהֲבוֹ נִפְרָע מִמֶּנּוּ מְעַט מְעַט;
— from his friend he collects little by little;
וְגַם לְעוֹרֵר עַל לְהַבָּא,
— and also to awaken him for the future,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חוֹשֵׂךְ שִׁבְטוֹ שׂוֹנֵא בְנוֹ וְגוֹמֵר וְאֹהֲבוֹ שִׁחֲרוֹ מוּסָר",
— as it is stated: 'He who spares his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him early,'
וְנֶאֱמַר: "כִּי אֶת אֲשֶׁר יֶאֱהַב ה' יוֹכִיחַ וּכְאָב וְגוֹמֵר".
— and it is stated: 'For whom Hashem loves He reproves, even as a father, etc.'
וְקָרְבָּנוֹת גַּם כֵּן מְכַפְּרִין עַל הֶעָבָר,
— And sacrifices likewise atone for the past,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פִּינְחָס):
— and as stated (Midrash Rabbah, Pinchas):
לֹא הָיָה אָדָם בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם וּבְיָדוֹ עָוֹן,
— no person remained in Jerusalem with a sin in his hand,
תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר מְכַפֵּר וְגוֹמֵר;
— the morning daily offering atoned, etc.;
וְעַל לְהַבָּא, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מִתְקָרֵב לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— and for the future, through this one draws close to Hashem, blessed be He,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זְבָחִים ז:):
— and in the manner they said (Zevachim 7b):
"רִצָּה פְּרַקְלִיט נִכְנָס דּוֹרוֹן אַחֲרָיו".
— ‘once the advocate has appeased, the gift enters after him’.
וְגַם דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל יֵצֶר הָרָע: הַיּוֹם כו' וּלְמָחָר אוֹמֵר לוֹ עֲשֵׂה כָּךְ כו'
— Moreover, such is the way of the evil inclination: today it says... and tomorrow it says do thus...
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שַׁבָּת קה:),
— (as stated in Shabbat 105b),
וּבַתְּחִלָּה קְרָאוֹ הֵלֶךְ וּלְבַסּוֹף קְרָאוֹ אוֹרֵחַ וְכוּלֵי,
— and at first Scripture calls it a traveler, and ultimately calls it a guest, etc.,
וּמוֹשֵׁךְ הֶעָוֹן בְּחַבְלֵי הַשָּׁוְא עַד שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ כַּעֲבוֹתוֹת הָעֲגָלָה
— and one draws sin with cords of vanity until afterward it becomes thick like wagon ropes
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר סֻכָּה נב:),
— (as stated in Sukkah 52b),
דַּעֲבֵירָה גּוֹרֶרֶת עֲבֵירָה,
— for transgression draws transgression,
וְעָבַר וְשָׁנָה נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר (יוֹמָא פו:);
— and once one commits a sin and repeats it, it seems to him as permitted (Yoma 86b);
וּכְשֶׁנִּמְחַל הַקּוֹדֵם עַל יְדֵי קָרְבָּן,
— and when the prior sin is forgiven through a sacrifice,
לֹא יוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו.
— the inclination cannot overpower him.
וְתוֹרָה הוּא עִיקַּר הַתַּבְלִין:
— And Torah is the essential antidote:
"מָשְׁכֵהוּ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ".
— ‘drag him to the study hall’.
וּתְפִלָּה – עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ:
— And prayer—based on what they said:
שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזְרוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ;
— that without the Holy One helping him, he could not overcome it;
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּכָן לַעֲזוֹר לְכָל אֶחָד,
— and Hashem stands ready to assist each individual,
רַק שֶׁהָאָדָם יִתְפַּלֵּל לוֹ עַל זֶה.
— provided that man prays to Him for this.
וְאִם הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין תְּשׁוּבָה,
— And had they repented,
הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ מוֹרִיד לָהֶם הַתּוֹרָה,
— Moses our teacher would have brought down the Torah to them,
וְהָיָה נֶהֶפָךְ לָהֶם מֵי הַמַּבּוּל לְמַיִם דְּתוֹרָה;
— and the waters of the Flood would have turned for them into the waters of Torah;
וְהֵם לֹא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל הָאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים,
— yet they refused to accept these four things,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה שָׁם מִן הַכָּתוּב:
— and as stated in Midrash Rabbah there from the verse:
"וַיֹּאמְרוּ לָאֵל סוּר מִמֶּנּוּ וְגוֹמֵר",
— ‘And they said to God: Depart from us, etc.’,
שֶׁמְּרַמֵּז שָׁם כָּל הָאַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים.
— all four of the aforementioned things being hinted at there.

paragraphs.text: Zevachim 7b: ‘This last statement of Rava is also taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon said: For what purpose is a sin offering brought? The Gemara interrupts: For what purpose is it brought? Is it not brought to atone for a transgression? Rather, Rabbi Shimon clearly meant: For what reason is it brought before a burnt offering in all circumstances where both are brought? Rabbi Shimon answered: It is comparable to an advocate [lifraklit] who enters before the king to convince him to pardon the defendant. Once the advocate has appeased the king, the gift is brought in after him.’

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 105b:8: “The Gemara asks: Say that you heard that Rabbi Yehuda rules that one is liable for performing a labor not needed for its own sake in the case of a constructive act; did you hear him deem one liable in the case of a destructive act? Rabbi Avin said: This case, where one rends his garment in anger, is also constructive, because in doing so he assuages his anger. Rending his garment calms him; therefore, it can be said that he derives benefit from the act of rending, and it is consequently a constructive act. The Gemara asks: And is it at all permitted to tear in that manner? Wasn’t it taught in a baraita that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Ḥilfa bar Agra, who said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri: One who rends his garments in his anger, or who breaks his vessels in his anger, or who scatters his money in his anger, should be like an idol worshipper in your eyes, as that is the craft of the evil inclination. Today it tells him do this, and tomorrow it tells him do that, until eventually, when he no longer controls himself, it tells him worship idols and he goes and worships idols. Rabbi Avin said: What verse alludes to this? “There shall not be a strange god within you, and you shall not bow to a foreign god” (Psalms 81:10). What is the strange god that is within a person’s body? Say that it is the evil inclination. One may not rend his garments in anger, because in doing so he is deriving pleasure from satisfying the evil inclination.”

h: The Souls of the Flood Generation Reborn in Egypt

p: וְאִיתָא בְּכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
— And it is brought in the writings of the Ari of blessed memory,
שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם בַּעֲבוֹדַת הַפֶּרֶךְ וְשֶׁקִּבְּלוּ אֶת הַתּוֹרָה
— that the souls of Israel who were in Egypt under backbreaking labor and who received the Torah,
הֵם הָיוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וּמִדּוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה,
— were the souls from the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion,
שֶׁהָיוּ בֵּינֵיהֶם נְפָשׁוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת,
— among whom were great souls,
רַק שֶׁהָיוּ מְעוֹרָבִים טוֹב וָרָע יַחַד.
— only that good and evil were intermingled within them.
כִּי מֵאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת
— For from the eating of the Tree of Knowledge
נַעֲשָׂה הָעִרְבּוּב גַּם בַּנְּשָׁמוֹת,
— the intermingling occurred within souls as well,
וְגַם הַנְּשָׁמָה הַטְּהוֹרָה הָיְתָה מְעוֹרֶבֶת עִם הַפְּחוּתָה,
— and even the pure soul was mixed with the lower one,
עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
— until Abraham our father came
וְזָכָה לִהְיוֹת אָב לְנִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and merited to be the father of the souls of Israel,
וְאָז נִבְדְּלוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַטְּהוֹרוֹת, נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, לְאוֹצָר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן,
— and then the pure souls, the souls of Israel, were separated into a treasury of their own,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה.)
— as written in Tosafot (Avodah Zarah 5a)
דְּ"עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף"
— that 'until all the souls in Guf are completed'—
הֵם נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם בְּאוֹצָר מְיוּחָד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— refers to the souls of Israel which reside in a unique treasury of their own, see there.
וְהִנֵּה מַה שֶּׁגָּרַם לְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל לִהְיוֹת "רַבָּה רָעַת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ",
— Now behold, what caused the Generation of the Flood to have 'the wickedness of man great in the earth',
הָיָה מֵרוֹב טוֹבַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם,
— was due to the abundance of worldly good they possessed,
וְלֹא הָיָה עֲלֵיהֶם עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְלֹא עוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ;
— having neither the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven nor the yoke of worldly labor;
כִּי לֹא נִצְרְכוּ גַּם לַעֲבוֹד בַּשָּׂדֶה,
— for they did not even need to toil in the field,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לד)
— as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 34)
דְּאַחַת לְאַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה הָיוּ זוֹרְעִים,
— that once every forty years they would sow,
וְהָיוּ רַק אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּפוֹחֲזִים,
— and they were merely eating, drinking, and acting frivolously,
וְרוֹב הַשַּׁלְוָה הֱבִיאָם שֶׁיִּמְרְדוּ וְיֶחֶטְאוּ
— and excess ease brought them to rebel and sin
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין קח.);
— (as written in Sanhedrin 108a);
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ גַּבֵּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— and so we find regarding Abraham our father,
כְּשֶׁעָבַר בִּמְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים וּפוֹחֲזִים
— when he traversed places where people were eating, drinking, and acting frivolously,
אָמַר: "הַלְּוַאי לֹא יְהֵא לִי חֵלֶק בָּאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת"
— he said: 'May it be that I have no portion in this land'
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לט),
— (as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 39),
כִּי דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ קָדְמָה לַתּוֹרָה,
— because worldly occupation precedes Torah,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁחוֹרְשִׁין בִּשְׁעַת חֲרִישָׁה וְכוּלֵי,
— in that through plowing during the plowing season, etc.,
הַיְגִיעָה בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ גַּם כֵּן מְשַׁכַּחַת עָוֹן;
— toil in worldly occupation likewise makes one forget sin;
וּכְשֶׁאֵין עוֹסְקִים בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וּמְבַלִּים בְּטוֹב יְמֵיהֶם בְּתַעֲנוּגֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
— and when people do not engage in labor and spend their days in ease amidst worldly pleasures,
זֶה מֵבִיא לִידֵי חֵטְא.
— this brings directly unto sin.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 34:11: ““As long as the earth endures, sowing and reaping, cold and heat, summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease” (Genesis 8:22). “As long as the earth endures, sowing and reaping, cold and heat…” – Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Shmuel: What do the descendants of Noah believe? That the covenant made with them will last forever? The truth is, rather, that as long as the heavens and the earth endure, their covenant is in effect. When that day comes regarding which it is written: “For the heavens will be eroded like smoke and the earth will wear away like a garment” (Isaiah 51:6), at that time: “It will be annulled on that day…” (Zechariah 11:11). Rabbi Aḥa said: [God said:] ‘What caused them [the generation of the Flood] to rebel against Me? Is it not because they would sow, but would not reap, bearing children and never burying them? From now forward: “sowing and reaping” – they will [sometimes] bear children and bury them; “cold and heat” – there will be fever and chills; “summer and winter” – I will bring birds to prey upon them in the summer, just as it says: “The bird of prey will prey on them in the summer, and all the beasts of the earth will prey on them in the winter” (Isaiah 18:6). There was an incident involving one of the prominent leaders of the generation who suffered from a headache. Some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman. He would say: Look at what the generation of the Flood brought upon us. Another interpretation, “as long as the earth endures” – Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Aḥa: What do the descendants of Noah believe? That the covenant made with them will last forever? This is what I said to them: “As long as the earth endures” – the truth is, rather, that as long as day and night endure, their covenant is in effect, but when that day comes regarding which it is written: “There will be one day, it will be known to the Lord, that is not day and not night” (Zechariah 14:7), at that moment: “It will be annulled on that day…” (Zechariah 11:11). Rabbi Yitzḥak said: [God said:] ‘What caused them to rebel against Me? Is it not because they would sow, but would not reap, as Rabbi Yitzḥak said: ‘Once in forty years they would need to sow’? And they were able to walk from one end of the earth to the other end in a short time, uprooting cedars of Lebanon with their feet [as they walked]. [Bites of] lions and leopards seemed to them like [tearing out] a hair from one’s flesh. And how pleasant was the weather for them? It was [eternally pleasant,] as it is between Passover and Shavuot. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Meir, and, likewise, Rabbi Dosa used to say in accordance with his opinion: Half of Tishrei, Marḥeshvan and Kislev – that is “sowing”; half of Kislev, Tevet, and half of Shevat – “winter”; half of Shevat, Adar, and half of Nisan – “cold”; half of Nisan, Iyar, and half of Sivan – “reaping”; half of Sivan, Tamuz, and half of Av – summer; half of Av, Elul, and half of Tishrei – “heat.” Rabbi Yehuda counts [these six seasons] from [the beginning of] Marḥeshvan. Rabbi Shimon begins [the count] with [the beginning of] Tishrei. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The constellations did not function all twelve months [of the Flood]. Rabbi Yonatan said to him: They functioned, but their effect was not palpable. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Eliezer says: “Shall not cease” means that they did not cease [during the Flood either]. Rabbi Yehoshua says: “Shall not cease” implies that they did cease [during the Flood].”

h: The Covenant and the Redemption of the Flood Generation

p: וְהִנֵּה יָדוּעַ שֶׁעִיקַּר חֵטְא דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
— Now behold, it is known that the primary sin of the Generation of the Flood
הָיָה בְּיוֹתֵר בְּעִנְיַן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— lay predominantly in the blemish of the Covenant (immorality),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי הִשְׁחִית כָּל בָּשָׂר וְגוֹמֵר";
— as it is stated: 'for all flesh had corrupted its way, etc.';
וְאַבְרָהָם יָדַע שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ יִהְיוּ מֵהַנְּפָשׁוֹת מִדּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
— and Abraham knew that his seed would stem from the souls of the Generation of the Flood
שֶׁנִּכְשְׁלוּ בַּעֲוֹן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית,
— who stumbled in the sin of blemish of the Covenant,
וְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינֶנָּה סוֹבֶלֶת אֲנָשִׁים חוֹטְאִים כָּאֵלֶּה,
— and the Land of Israel does not tolerate such sinners,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִזְהִירָה תּוֹרָה:
— as the Torah warned:
"כְּמַעֲשֵׂה אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם וְגוֹמֵר לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ",
— ‘After the doings of the land of Egypt, etc., shall you not do’,
"וְלֹא תָקִיא הָאָרֶץ אֶתְכֶם וְגוֹמֵר";
— ‘that the land vomit you not out, etc.’;
וּמַעֲשֵׂה אֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁטוּפִים בִּזְנוּת,
— and the doings of Egypt meant they were immersed in licentiousness,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "אֲשֶׁר בְּשַׂר חֲמוֹרִים בְּשָׂרָם וְזִרְמַת סוּסִים זִרְמָתָם".
— as stated: 'whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.'
וְעַל כֵּן כְּשֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
— Therefore, when the Holy One, blessed be He, told him:
"אֲנִי ה' וְגוֹמֵר לָתֶת לְךָ אֶת הָאָרֶץ הַזֹּאת לְרִשְׁתָּהּ",
— ‘I am Hashem, etc., to give you this land to inherit it’,
שָׁאַל: "בַּמָּה אֵדַע כִּי אִירָשֶׁנָּה".
— he asked: 'Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?'
שֶׁאַף שֶׁהֶאֱמִין שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי יִתֵּן ה' הָאָרֶץ לְזַרְעוֹ,
— For even though he believed that Hashem would certainly give the land to his seed,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם שָׁאַל: "בַּמָּה אֵדַע שֶׁיִּתְקַיְּמוּ בָּהּ",
— nonetheless he asked: 'Whereby shall I know that they will endure within it?'
בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ יִתְגַּבְּרוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשְׁלוּ עוֹד בַּעֲוֹן דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
— Through what power will they overcome so as not to stumble again in the sin of the Flood generation,
וְלֹא תָקִיא הָאָרֶץ אוֹתָם,
— that the land should not vomit them out,
וְתִהְיֶה לָהֶם הָאָרֶץ לִירוּשָׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק.
— and that the land be unto them an everlasting inheritance?
וְעַל זֶה הֱשִׁיבוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ:
— And to this Hashem answered him:
"כִּי גֵר יִהְיֶה זַרְעֲךָ וְגוֹמֵר וַעֲבָדוּם וְעִנּוּ אֹתָם",
— ‘That your seed shall be a stranger, etc., and they shall serve them, and they shall afflict them’,
וְעַל יְדֵי הָעַבְדוּת וְהָעִינּוּי
— and through servitude and affliction
יִתְבָּרְרוּ וְיִתְלַבְּנוּ מֵחֵטְא דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל;
— they will be clarified and cleansed from the sin of the Flood generation;
כִּי בְּחֵטְא פְּגַם הַבְּרִית הַמִּשְׁפָּט לִהְיוֹת עֶבֶד,
— for regarding the sin of blemish of the Covenant the judgment is to become a slave,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּהַשְּׁבָטִים דְּדָנוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף לְמָכְרוֹ לְעֶבֶד.
— just as we found regarding the tribes who judged Joseph to sell him as a slave.
וְהוּא הָיָה שׁוֹרֶשׁ קְדוּשַׁת הַבְּרִית,
— Now he was the root of the holiness of the Covenant,
אֲבָל הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְבֵירוּרִים,
— yet he required refinements,
כִּי הֵם חֲשָׁדוּהוּ לְהֵיפֶךְ
— since they suspected him of the reverse,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוֹצִיא לַעַז עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין עֵינֵיהֶם בִּבְנוֹת הָאָרֶץ,
— because he brought an evil report about them that they cast their eyes upon the daughters of the land;
וְהֵם יָדְעוּ שֶׁנְּקִיִּים מִזֶּה,
— and they knew within themselves that they were pure of this,
אָמְרוּ שֶׁ"בְּמוּמוֹ פּוֹסֵל"
— so they said that 'one who invalidates others disqualifies through his own blemish',
וּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ מֵחִסָּרוֹן זֶה.
— and certainly he harbors this flaw.
וּכְדִאִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה פד):
— And as brought (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 84):
אָמְרוּ: נֵלֵךְ וְנִתְפּוֹס דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם,
— They said: Let us go and follow the way of the world;
כְּנַעַן שֶׁחָטָא, לֹא לְעֶבֶד נִתְקַלֵּל?
— Canaan who sinned, was he not cursed to be a slave?
וְחֵטְא כְּנַעַן הָיָה בִּפְגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁפָּגַם חָם
— And the sin of Canaan was in blemish of the Covenant which Ham committed
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר סַנְהֶדְרִין ע. קח:);
— (as stated in Sanhedrin 70a, 108b);
אַף זֶה, לְכוּ וְנִמְכְּרֶנּוּ.
— this one too—come, let us sell him!
וְנִמְכַּר לְמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהִיא מְקוֹם הַזִּימָּה,
— And he was sold to Egypt, which was the epicenter of licentiousness,
וְשָׁם נִתְבָּרֵר עַל יְדֵי הַנִּסָּיוֹן שֶׁהוּא נָקִי וּמוּגְדָּר,
— and there he was proven through trial to be pure and guarded,
וְנִגְדְּרוּ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּזְכוּתוֹ
— and all of Israel were fenced against immorality in his merit,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, יב).
— as our Sages of blessed memory taught (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12).
וּמִצְרַיִם "עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ",
— And Egypt was 'the nakedness of the earth',
וּלְשָׁם גָּלוּ לְבָרֵר שֶׁהֵם נְקִיִּים בָּזֶה;
— and thither they were exiled to demonstrate that they were completely pure in this;
וּכְשֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר זֶה נִגְאָלִין,
— and when this was clarified, they were redeemed,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה שָׁם)
— as stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah there)
דְּנִגְאֲלוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוּרִים בַּעֲרָיוֹת.
— that they were redeemed from Egypt because they were strictly guarded against forbidden relations.
וְעַל יְדֵי הָעַבְדוּת וְהָעִינּוּי
— And through servitude and affliction
תִּקְּנוּ חֵטְא דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל,
— they rectified the sin of the Generation of the Flood,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— and as the Ari of blessed memory wrote

— that for souls from the Flood generation it was decreed: 'Every son that is born you shall cast into the river',

— and Moses our teacher rescued them,

— as stated (Sotah 12b):

— Moses said to them: 'For my sake were you all saved.'

— And for the souls from the Generation of the Dispersion
עָבְדוּ בָּהֶם "בְּחֹמֶר וּבִלְבֵנִים".

— they no longer required servitude and affliction,

— only to be toiling in Torah

— and to undergo the rigors of Torah.

— And in place of their toil in the bondage of mortar and bricks,

— and what they suffered from being cast into the river,

— they merited afterward the waters of Torah

— and the analytical reasoning of the Oral Torah through a fortiori arguments (kal va-chomer) and clarifying halakhot (libbun hilkhata).

— And counter to the Tower of Babel

— they merited Jerusalem and the Holy Temple.

— And that which the Generation of the Dispersion used unity and peace to rebel against the Omnipresent,

— they merited afterward, once refined, the dialectic of Torah,

— concerning which it is written: 'et vahev be-sufah'—
שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת הַפִּלְפּוּל נִרְאִים הַתַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים כְּאוֹיְבִים זֶה לָזֶה
— that during the dialectic debate Torah scholars appear like enemies to one another,

— yet do not depart from there until they become beloved friends to one another

— (as stated in Kiddushin 30b)

— once the halakhah has been clarified to them.

— And this is why Midrash Tanchuma elaborated in this parashah
בִּשְׁבַח יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַתּוֹרָה,
— in praise of Israel and the Torah,
כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת מֵאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר וּמִנַּפְשׁוֹתֵיהֶם
— for in truth from that generation and from their souls

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 70a:19: “The Gemara explains: The one who says that Ham castrated Noah adduces the following proof: Since he injured Noah with respect to the possibility of conceiving a fourth son, which Noah wanted but could no longer have, therefore Noah cursed him by means of Ham’s fourth son. And the one who says that Ham sodomized Noah learned this from a verbal analogy between the words “and he saw” and “and he saw.” Here it is written: “And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father”; and there it is written: “And Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, and he took her, and lay with her, and afflicted her” (Genesis 34:2). This indicates that the term “saw” alludes to sexual intercourse.”

paragraphs.text: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12:1: ““A locked garden is my sister, my bride; a locked fountainhead, a sealed spring. Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates, with delicious fruit, henna with nard” (Song of Songs 4:12–13). “A locked garden is my sister, my bride” – Rabbi Yehuda ben Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: [This is analogous] to a king who had two daughters, one older and one younger, and he did not devote attention to arranging their marriages. The king left them for many years and went overseas. The girls arose and asserted themselves and married themselves to men. Each of them would take her husband’s seal and his signet. Years later, the king returned from overseas and he heard the voices of the people slandering his daughters and saying that the king’s daughters had engaged in licentiousness. What did he do? He issued a proclamation and said: The entire people shall go out to the assembly hall. He came and sat in the vestibule. He said to them: ‘My daughters, is this what you have done; have you tainted yourselves?’ Immediately, each of them produced her husband’s seal and his signet. He called his son-in-law and said to him: ‘To whom are you a bridegroom?’ He said to him: ‘I am your first son-in-law, [married] to your older daughter.’ He said to him: ‘What is this?’ He said to him: ‘This is my seal and this is my signet,’ and likewise [occurred with] the second [son-in-law]. At that moment, the king said: My daughters are sheltered from immorality and you slander and demean them? By your lives, I will administer justice against you. So it is with the nations, because they would taunt Israel and say: “Egypt enslaved the children of Israel [with harshness]” (Exodus 1:13); if they compelled them to perform labor, all the more so [they must have dominated] their bodies and their wives. At that moment, the Holy One blessed be He said: My sister, My bride, a locked garden. What is a locked garden? The Holy One blessed be He said: My garden is locked and it is being condemned? Rabbi Pinḥas said: At that moment the Holy One blessed be He called the angel appointed over pregnancy and said: Go and shape [the children] with all the features of their fathers. Who did the fathers themselves resemble? The paterfamilias of the families. That is what is written regarding Reuben: “The families of the Reubenites [haReuveni]” (Numbers 26:7). Rabbi Hoshaya said: Reuben, Reubenite [haReuveni], Simeon, Simeonite [haShimoni]. Rabbi Marinos ben Rabbi Hoshaya said: Like you say: Baronite, Savronite, Sivoyite. Rabbi Huna in the name of Rabbi Idi: Heh at the beginning of the word and yod at the end; God [yod-heh] attests for them that they were indeed the sons of their fathers. Rabbi Pinḥas said: “A locked garden” – these are the virgins. “A locked fountainhead” – these are the non-virgins. “A sealed spring” – these are the males. It was taught in the name of Rabbi Natan: “A locked garden, a locked fountainhead” – why was it [written] twice? Rather, it connotes two acts of intercourse for the woman; one in the typical manner and one in the atypical manner. Rabbi Huna said in the name of bar Kappara: By virtue of four matters, Israel was redeemed from Egypt: That they did not change their name, they did not change their language, they did not speak slander, and not one of them was steeped in licentiousness. They did not change their name: Reuben and Simeon descended [to Egypt]; Reuben and Simeon ascended. They did not call Reuben Rufus, they did not call Simeon Luleyani, Joseph, Listis, or Benjamin, Alexandra. They did not change their language. There, it is written: “The survivor came and told Abram the Hebrew” (Genesis 14:13), and here it is written: “The God of the Hebrews has called upon us” (Exodus 5:3), and it is written: “That it is my mouth speaking to you” (Genesis 45:12), in the sacred tongue. They did not speak slander, as it is stated: “Speak now in the ears of the people, and let them ask each man from his neighbor” (Exodus 11:2). You find that this matter had been entrusted to them for twelve months, and not one of them was found to have informed on his counterpart. Not one of them was steeped in licentiousness, as it is stated: “The son of an Israelite woman, [whose father was an Egyptian.…] the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed” (Leviticus 24:10–11), to apprise in praise of Israel that not one of them was found except for this one, and the verse publicized her. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Sarah descended to Egypt and sheltered herself from licentiousness, and all the [Israelite] women were sheltered by her merit. Joseph descended to Egypt and sheltered himself from licentiousness, and all the males were sheltered by his merit. Rabbi Pinḥas in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya: The sheltering from licentiousness was itself sufficient that by its merit Israel would have been redeemed from Egypt. What is the reason? “A locked garden is my sister, my bride.” What is written thereafter? “Your branches [shelaḥayikh] are an orchard of pomegranates.” Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai taught: [This is analogous] to one to whom an inheritance fell at the site of a garbage dump. The heir was indolent and he sold it at a minimal price. The purchaser went and industriously excavated there and found a treasure. He built a large palace. The purchaser began walking in the marketplace with servants following him [all due] to the treasure that he had purchased there. The seller saw and was sorrowful, saying: Woe is me over what I lost. So too, when Israel was in Egypt, they were enslaved in mortar and bricks and they were contemptible in the eyes of the Egyptians. When they saw their flags encamped at the sea in the array of a royal army, the Egyptians became sorrowful, saying: Woe are we, what did we send from our land? This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17). Rabbi Yonatan said: [This is analogous] to one who had a field capable of producing a kor, and he went and sold it at a minimal price. The purchaser went and excavated springs and planted gardens and orchards there. The seller saw and was sorrowful, saying: Woe is me over what I lost. So too, when Israel was in Egypt, they were enslaved in mortar and bricks and they were contemptible in the eyes of the Egyptians. When they saw their flags encamped at the sea in the array of a royal army, the Egyptians became sorrowful, saying: Woe are we, what did we send from our land? This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17). Rabbi Yosei said: [This is analogous] to one who had chopped-down cedars, and he sold it at a minimal price. The purchaser went and crafted from them trunks, closets, chests, and wagons. The seller saw and was sorrowful, saying: Woe is me over what I lost. So too, when Israel was in Egypt, they were enslaved in mortar and bricks and they were contemptible in the eyes of the Egyptians. When they saw their flags encamped at the sea in the array of a royal army, the Egyptians became sorrowful, saying: Woe are we, what did we send from our land? This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17).”

Rather, it connotes two acts of intercourse for the woman; one in the typical manner and one in the atypical manner. They did not call Reuben Rufus, they did not call Simeon Luleyani, Joseph, Listis, or Benjamin, Alexandra. They did not change their language. They did not speak slander, as it is stated: “Speak now in the ears of the people, and let them ask each man from his neighbor” (Exodus 11:2). You find that this matter had been entrusted to them for twelve months, and not one of them was found to have informed on his counterpart. This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17). Rabbi Yonatan said: [This is analogous] to one who had a field capable of producing a kor, and he went and sold it at a minimal price. The purchaser went and excavated springs and planted gardens and orchards there. The seller saw and was sorrowful, saying: Woe is me over what I lost. So too, when Israel was in Egypt, they were enslaved in mortar and bricks and they were contemptible in the eyes of the Egyptians. When they saw their flags encamped at the sea in the array of a royal army, the Egyptians became sorrowful, saying: Woe are we, what did we send from our land? This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17). Rabbi Yosei said: [This is analogous] to one who had chopped-down cedars, and he sold it at a minimal price. The purchaser went and crafted from them trunks, closets, chests, and wagons. The seller saw and was sorrowful, saying: Woe is me over what I lost. So too, when Israel was in Egypt, they were enslaved in mortar and bricks and they were contemptible in the eyes of the Egyptians. When they saw their flags encamped at the sea in the array of a royal army, the Egyptians became sorrowful, saying: Woe are we, what did we send from our land? This is as it is stated: “It was [vayhi] when Pharaoh sent” (Exodus 13:17).”

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 30b:2: “The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of the phrase “enemies in the gate” with regard to Torah study? Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says: Even a father and his son, or a rabbi and his student, who are engaged in Torah together in one gate become enemies with each other due to the intensity of their studies. But they do not leave there until they love each other, as it is stated in the verse discussing the places the Jewish people engaged in battle in the wilderness: “Therefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord, Vahev in Suphah [beSufa], and the valleys of Arnon” (Numbers 21:14). The word “vahev” is interpreted as related to the word for love, ahava. Additionally, do not read this as “in Suphah [beSufa]”; rather, read it as “at its end [besofa],” i.e., at the conclusion of their dispute they are beloved to each other.”

h: The Midrash on the Spiritual Purpose of Suffering

p: וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּונַת הַמִּדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא בְּמַה שֶׁכָּתַב:
— And this is likewise the intent of Midrash Tanchuma in what it wrote:
"אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ,
— ‘These are the generations of Noah—
כָּךְ פָּתַח רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא בַּר אַבָּא:
— so opened Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba:
'פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים' וְגוֹמֵר,
— "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, etc." (Proverbs 11:30);
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָדָם מִסְתַּלֵּק מִן הָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא בָּנִים הוּא מֵיצַר,
— when a man departs from the world without children he is sorrowful;
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵי:
— the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, etc.:
יֵשׁ לְךָ פְּרִי יָפֶה מִן הַבָּנִים וְכוּלֵי
— You have a fruit more beautiful than children, etc.—
הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ: 'פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים',
— the Torah, concerning which it is written: "The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life",
'בָּנִים' אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר וְכוּלֵי".
— 'children' it does not say, etc.’
וְלִכְאוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר "אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ וְגוֹמֵר",
— And seemingly it bears no relevance to that which is stated: 'These are the generations of Noah, etc.',
שֶׁהֲרֵי נֹחַ הָיָה לוֹ בָּנִים
— for behold, Noah had children
וְכָל הָעוֹלָם יָצְאוּ מִזַּרְעוֹ!
— and the entire world emerged from his seed!
וּכְשֶׁרָצְתָה הַתּוֹרָה לְרַמֵּז שֶׁעִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם מַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים,
— And when the Torah wished to hint that a person's primary offspring are his good deeds,
הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַמֵּז בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּת בְּלֹא בָּנִים,
— it ought to have hinted this regarding one who died childless,
וְלֹא בְּנֹחַ שֶׁהִנִּיחַ בָּנִים!
— and not regarding Noah, who left behind children!
אָמְנָם בָּא לְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִטְעֶה,
— However, it comes to teach us lest we err,
מֵאַחַר שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר רַק נֹחַ וְזַרְעוֹ
— that since only Noah and his seed survived
וְהוּא הָאָב שֶׁל כָּל הָעוֹלָם,
— and he is the father of the whole world,
הֵם נֶחְשְׁבוּ תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו
— they should be considered his true descendants—
כִּי לֹא כֵן הוּא;
— for this is not so;
שֶׁהֵם שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ בְּנֵי נֹחַ
— for those who are called 'the descendants of Noah' (Bnei Noach)
אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְקַבָּלַת הַתּוֹרָה וּלְמִצְווֹת וּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— have no connection to the reception of the Torah, the mitzvot, and the holiness of Shabbat;
וְאַדְּרַבָּה, נֶאֱמַר לָהֶם: "וְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה לֹא יִשְׁבֹּתוּ",
— and on the contrary, it was said to them: 'and day and night they shall not cease',
כִּי בִּמְנוּחָתָם וּשְׁבִיתָתָם יוֹסִיפוּ לַחֲטֹא מִתּוֹךְ הַבַּטָּלָה.
— because through their leisure and cessation from work they would add sin through idleness.
וְזֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ כְּלָל,
— And the seed of Israel are not named after him at all,
דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ הָיָה תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים,
— for Abraham our father was the first of proselytes,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (חֲגִיגָה ג.),
— as stated (Chagigah 3a),
וְגֵר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי
— and a convert who undergoes conversion is like a newborn child
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יְבָמוֹת כב.),
— (as stated in Yevamot 22a),
וְהוּא זָכָה לִהְיוֹת אָב רִאשׁוֹן לְכָל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
— and he merited to be the first father to all souls of Israel.
וְנִפְרְשׁוּ בְּאוֹצָר מְיוּחָד הַנְּשָׁמוֹת מְקַבְּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה,
— And the souls that were to receive the Torah were set aside in a unique treasury,
וְעִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹת נֹחַ הוּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "נֹחַ אִישׁ צַדִּיק תָּמִים",
— and the essential generations of Noah are that which is written: 'Noah was a righteous, wholehearted man',
שֶׁתּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם אֵלּוּ מַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים.
— for a person's real descendants are his good deeds.
וּבָא לְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁאַף מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים יֵדַע שֶׁאֵין זֶה עִיקַּר הַתַּכְלִית,
— And it comes to teach us that even one who has children should know that this is not the ultimate purpose,
וְיִרְאֶה שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה פְּרִי הַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְווֹת שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ "פְּרִי צַדִּיק עֵץ חַיִּים",
— and should see to bear the fruit of Torah and mitzvot which are termed 'the fruit of the righteous is a tree of life',
וְהֵם תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
— and they are a person's true generations.

h: Earlier Generations Redeemed Through Later Merit

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַסִּיק בַּמִּדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא:
— And afterward it concludes in Midrash Tanchuma:
"וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאַף לָרִאשׁוֹנִים בִּזְכוּת אַחֲרוֹנִים?
— ‘And whence do we know that even the early ones were saved in the merit of the later ones?
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'וְנֹחַ מָצָא חֵן וְגוֹמֵר',
— For it is said: "And Noah found grace, etc.";
בְּאֵיזֶה זְכוּת? בִּזְכוּת תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו,
— by what merit? In the merit of his generations,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת נֹחַ'".
— as it is said: "These are the generations of Noah".’
וְכֵן כָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת בְּרֵאשִׁית כט, ה) וְשָׁם פָּרָשָׁה כו (כו, ו):
— And so is written in Midrash Rabbah (end of Parashat Bereishit 29:5) and there in Parashah 26 (26:6):
לֹא שֶׁהָיָה כְּדַאי,
— not that he was personally worthy,
אֶלָּא שֶׁצָּפָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה עָתִיד לַעֲמוֹד מִמֶּנּוּ.
— rather the Holy One foresaw that Moses was destined to arise from him.
וְנִרְאֶה לִכְאוֹרָה סְתִירָה מֵרֹאשׁוֹ לְסוֹפוֹ,
— And seemingly there appears a contradiction from its beginning to its end,
שֶׁבַּפֶּתַח שֶׁתּוֹלְדוֹתָיו מַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים הֵם!
— for at the opening it stated that his generations are his good deeds!
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עַל נֹחַ:
— However in truth they stated in Bereishit Rabbah regarding Noah:
"בְּדֹרֹתָיו" – בְּדוֹרוֹתָיו הָיָה צַדִּיק,
— ‘in his generations’—in his generations he was righteous,
הָא אִילּוּ הָיָה בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵי לֹא הָיָה צַדִּיק.
— yet had he lived in the generation of Moses, etc., he would not have been considered righteous.
וְנִמְלַט רַק בִּזְכוּת שֶׁיָּצָא מִמֶּנּוּ אוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית מְקַבְּלֵי הַתּוֹרָה וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
— And he was rescued solely in the merit that from him would issue the Jewish nation, receivers of the Torah, and Moses our teacher, and the like.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמֵּהַהֶכְרֵחַ שֶׁיּוּשְׁאַר אֶחָד לְקִיּוּם הָעוֹלָם שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
— And since it was necessary that one survive for the preservation of the world so that they emerge from him,
נִשְׁאַר הוּא שֶׁהָיָה צַדִּיק בְּדוֹרוֹתָיו.
— he remained, who was righteous in his generations.
אֲבָל בָּאָה הַתּוֹרָה לְלַמְּדֵנוּ
— However the Torah came to teach us
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הַצַּדִּיקִים לֹא נִקְרְאוּ עַל שְׁמוֹ,
— that in truth the righteous are not called after his name,
שֶׁהֵם נִקְרָאִים בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד,
— for they are called the children of Abraham who was like a newborn child;
וְהַנּוֹדֵר מִבְּנֵי נֹחַ מוּתָּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
— and one who vows not to benefit from the descendants of Noah may benefit from Jews,
כֵּיוָן דְּאִיקַּדַּשׁ אַבְרָהָם אִתְקְרוּ עַל שְׁמֵיהּ
— since once Abraham was sanctified they were designated after his name
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר נְדָרִים לא.);
— (as stated in Nedarim 31a);
וְעִיקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו מַה שֶּׁבֵּירֵר עַצְמוֹ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים,
— and his essential offspring was that which he refined himself in his good deeds,
שֶׁהֵן תּוֹלְדוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם;
— which are a person's true generations;
וּלְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁעִיקַּר הַפְּרִי הוּא עֵץ חַיִּים,
— and to teach us that the essential fruit is the tree of life,
שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
— which is words of Torah and good deeds.

h: The Torah as the Culmination of Divine Mercy

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ, אַחַר שֶׁהֶאֱרִיךְ בִּשְׁבַח הַתּוֹרָה,
— And afterward, having elaborated in praise of the Torah,
מְסַיֵּים בַּמִּדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא:
— it concludes in Midrash Tanchuma:
"וְכִי מִשּׁוּם דְּצַדִּיק ה' 'וַיִּשְׁקֹד עַל הָרָעָה'?
— ‘Is it because Hashem is righteous that "He watched over the evil"?
אֶלָּא צְדָקָה עָשָׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל
— Rather the Holy One, blessed be He, performed charity with Israel
שֶׁהִקְדִּים וְהִגְלָה אֶת גָּלוּת יְכָנְיָה לְגָלוּת צִדְקִיָּהוּ,
— by advancing and exiling the captivity of Jeconiah before the captivity of Zedekiah,
כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח מֵהֶן תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
— so that the Oral Torah should not be forgotten from them,
וְיָשְׁבוּ בְּתוֹרָתָן בְּבָבֶל עַד הַיּוֹם,
— and they sat with their Torah in Babylonia until this day,
וְלֹא שָׁלַט בָּהֶן לֹא עָוֹן וְכוּלֵי",
— and neither sin, etc., held dominion over them’;
כִּי עִיקַּר הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִתְחִיל אַחַר הַגָּלוּת,
— for the primary expansion of the Oral Torah began after the exile,
דְּ"כִּי בְּרֹב חָכְמָה רָב כָּעַס",
— for 'in much wisdom is much grief' (Ecclesiastes 1:18),
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָרַב כַּעַס נִתְרַבָּה הָרַב חָכְמָה.
— in that through much grief much wisdom was multiplied.
וְהָיוּ אָז אַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהִרְבּוּ חִדּוּדֵי תּוֹרָה,
— And then were the Men of the Great Assembly who multiplied sharp insights of Torah,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵן לֹא שָׁלְטוּ בָּהֶן,
— and through this sins did not dominate them,
שֶׁעִיקַּר הַשְּׁלִיטָה הָיָה לָהֶם מֵחֲמַת שֶׁמִּתְרַשְּׁלִין בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— for the primary dominion of sins occurred because they slackened in Torah,
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ כֹּחַ בַּיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְפַתּוֹת.
— and automatically the evil inclination gains power to seduce.
אָמְנָם הַמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל תּוֹרָה,
— However, one who takes upon himself the yoke of Torah—
דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה רְפוּאָה וְתִיקּוּן לְכָל עָוֹן וָחֵטְא;
— words of Torah are healing and rectification for every iniquity and sin;
וְאַף לִפְגַם הַבְּרִית שֶׁהֶחְמִיר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב),
— and even regarding the blemish of the Covenant, where the holy Zohar (Part I, 219b) was stringent,
כַּוָּונָתוֹ רַק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תִּיקּוּן לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהֶם זְכִיּוֹת;
— his intent was only that one cannot rectify it to transform intentional sins into merits;
אָמְנָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּבַתּוֹרָה מוֹעִיל שֶׁיִּנָּצֵל מֵעֹנֶשׁ עַל כָּל פָּנִים,
— nevertheless through repentance and Torah it avails to be spared from punishment at least,
וְלֹא תִזָּכַרְנָה הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת וְלֹא תַעֲלֶינָה עַל לֵב.
— and 'the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.'
